title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 85
paragraphs: He was buried, then, in some such manner. The Greeks, having divided the spoils at Plataea, proceeded to bury their dead, each nation apart. The Spartans made themselves three separate burial-places: in one they buried the younger Spartans, among whom were Poseidonios, Amompharetos, Philokyon, and Callicrates; in the second, the rest of the Spartans; in the third, the Helots. They then buried their dead thus. The Tegeans buried theirs together in a place apart from these; the Athenians, theirs together; the Megarians and Phliasians, those who had been killed by the cavalry. The burial-places of all these contained bodies; but as for the burial-places of other cities to be seen at Plataea, these, as I am told, are all merely mounds of earth without bodies in them, raised by the various peoples on account of posterity, because they were ashamed of their absence from the fight. Among others there is one called the burial-place of the Aeginetans, which I hear was raised at the request of the Aeginetans by Cleades son of Autodicos, a Plataean who was their public guest-friend, no less than ten years after these events.
